Apple has replaced a billboard in Milan showing a young child holding an iPhone, part of its latest "Relax, it's iPhone" campaign. Here's the full story.

Apple pulls controversial Italian billboard

Days ago, Italy's child welfare authority Autorità Garante per l'Infanzia e l'Adolescenza (AGIA) condemned Apple's use of a child holding an iPhone in imagery for its "Relax, it's iPhone" campaign.

The campaign primarily showcases the iPhone's durability, depicting the device in potentially damaging scenarios, including being used to take photos in heavy rain, balanced on the edge of a bathtub while playing video, gripped in a dog's mouth, and clumsily held by a young child.

After a billboard depicting the final scenario was erected on via Melchiorre Gioia in Milan, AGIA received a letter from a concerned citizen arguing the ad normalised the use of devices as an "electronic babysitter".

AGIA agreed, and referred the matter to Italian communications regulator AGCOM, Italian competition authority AGCM, and local advertising self-regulatory body IAP "for appropriate scrutiny and possible follow-up action".

Now, according to Prima Comunicazione and Repubblica Milano, Apple has pulled the controversial billboard, replacing it with an ad promoting its Find My feature.

Apple has not publicly responded to the episode, but the company's swift response reflects how seriously it takes such criticism—even though the ad was intended to highlight the iPhone's durability, it was read very differently.

What are your thoughts on this controversy? Let us know in the comments.
